to rising temperatures.

humid days. The temperature of the Earth is rising, and when

plain_text:
■ Heat cramps. These are muscle cramps, usually in the legs or
stomach, caused by loss of salt from sweating. If you start having
heat cramps, it's important to drink lots of fluids, especially those
with electrolytes. Also find a cooler space.
■ Heat exhaustion. Symptoms include heavy sweating, cold and
clammy skin, nausea, and vomiting.
■ Heat stroke. This is when your body temperature exceeds
104 degrees Fahrenheit (40 degrees Celsius). Heat stroke can
be life-threatening.
